items.title: 2 Industrials Stocks to Keep an Eye On and 1 We Turn Down
items.summary: Whether you see them or not, industrials businesses play a crucial part in our daily activities. Still, their generally high capital requirements expose them to the ups and downs of economic cycles, and the industry’s six-month return of 2.7% has fallen short of the S&P 500’s 18.4% rise.

items.title: Why Does Vertiv Cost The Most In A Group It Does Not Out-Grow?
items.summary: Vertiv (VRT) is the most expensive stock in its peer group, at 56.3 times earnings. It leads that group on neither revenue growth nor operating margin. What it does lead is the twelve-month return, up 76.7%. So the premium rests on the acceleration management has guided for the second half of 2026, not on what Vertiv has already earned.
